reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices quarterly report July 2023 - September 2023

description.narrative: Over the period, the program implemented various interventions that reached around 87780 using various platforms including 84,484 through the social media and around 3296 through various physical platforms including Art and sports dialogue forums that brought youth and leaders together to learn on the role of leaders, give feedback on service delivery and developed advocacy strategies aimed at addressing the concerns, Community vision building that brought together tertiary students and host community together to discuss on how they could collaborate in addressing issues affecting both students and the host community. The program also supported Gumzo mtaani aimed at creating youth awareness and increase their level of participation in the political processes and two intergenerational dialogue focusing on the secondary school leaders on their perspective on govern nave and service delivery and use of technology in facilitating youth participation in governance with the focus on reducing misinformation and disinformation. The forums created a platform for young people to engage with duty bearers and other stakeholders, improved their understanding on the constitutionally provided rights and strategies of demanding the rights. As a result, 9 governance issues that were raised, 2 were addressed while 7 issues are still under the advocacy follow up of the county based accountability champions The program however faced various challenges including slow responsive rate among the county based youth organizations tasked with the responsibility of implementing the agreed advocacy strategies and low capacity in the use of social media. Slow response on the part of government officials have also slowed the response rate on the issues that have been identified. To address the above challenges, the program will continue with the mentorship for both online and offline county based youth organizations (Count accountability champions), expand the reach for the county based youth organizations to reduce reliance on specific groups within the county and continue to invite government to the forums to ensure that they understand the importance of the forums created in their work
